evaluatedSources.name: Slippery Hill
evaluatedSources.context: Performer and edition details are retained when the source page provides them. Discovery/apply run against the full unresolved backlog by default (no small fixed batch limit).

evaluatedSources.name: Internet Archive
evaluatedSources.context: Review reports preserve the collection, file, rights/license, creator, performer when named, and source-page URL. There is no manual editorial 'is this a genuine old-time edition' gate — exact match, rights/license, attribution, and a verified playable file are sufficient to auto-attach. Discovery/apply run against the full unresolved backlog by default (no small fixed batch limit).

evaluatedSources.name: Wikimedia Commons
evaluatedSources.context: Commons only hosts freely licensed or public-domain media, but individual files can still declare restricted terms, so the license line is rechecked live before every apply.

evaluatedSources.name: Library of Congress
evaluatedSources.status: approved for direct audio when the live item API exposes a verified MP3; otherwise retained as a trusted archival reference
evaluatedSources.context: The loc.gov JSON API and tile.loc.gov MP3 resources are currently reachable. Archival references remain distinct from direct-audio coverage until the item-specific MP3 and rights checks pass. Existing references can be upgraded without replacing any other trusted recording.

evaluatedSources.name: Southern Folklife Collection / Digital SFC
evaluatedSources.status: evaluated, not approved for automated direct imports
evaluatedSources.context: The collection contains relevant field recordings, but search discovery alone is not enough evidence for automatic attachment. No lawful, scriptable per-file audio+rights endpoint was found during evaluation.

evaluatedSources.name: Smithsonian Folkways / Learning Lab
evaluatedSources.status: evaluated, not approved for automated direct imports
evaluatedSources.context: The Smithsonian Open Access API returns rich catalog metadata for Folkways recordings but no downloadable audio file for them (they are physical/commercial recordings, not digitized open-access media). Folkways.si.edu track pages offer short promotional preview clips only, sold under standard commercial terms rather than a redistributable license, so they do not clear the rights bar.

evaluatedSources.name: Folkstreams / NCTA
evaluatedSources.status: evaluated, not approved for automated direct imports
evaluatedSources.context: Folkstreams publishes documentary films (not individual tune tracks), and the site exposes no discoverable API for scripted per-title lookup, so exact tune-title matching and rights verification are not currently possible here.

evaluatedSources.name: Digital Library of Appalachia
evaluatedSources.status: evaluated, not approved for automated direct imports
evaluatedSources.context: The site runs on CONTENTdm; its dmwebservices API endpoint returned 403/blocked responses to automated requests during evaluation, and per-item rights statements vary by collection, so this lane cannot be verified end-to-end from the automated sourcing environment.

evaluatedSources.name: Berea College Sound Archives
evaluatedSources.status: evaluated, not approved for automated tune-level imports
evaluatedSources.context: The Preservica catalog and direct MP3 downloads are scriptable, and the Bruce Greene, John Harrod, Steve Rice, and Barbara Kunkle collections contain hundreds of relevant recordings. The exposed files are full cassettes or reels named for performers/interviews rather than individual tunes, and item pages state that material is posted for personal research and educational purposes. Treating an entire tape as one tune would be inaccurate, so this source remains a documented shortfall rather than a title-only import lane.

evaluatedSources.name: Duke Digital Collections
evaluatedSources.status: evaluated, not approved for automated direct imports
evaluatedSources.context: repository.duke.edu is protected by an interactive bot challenge that blocks scripted access, so item-level title, rights, and audio-file verification cannot be automated from this environment.

shortfall.explanation: The source records above quantify every approved lane as exhausted, paused, running, or not started. Rights-unclear, title-collision, blocked, and video-only media are not counted.
